raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t chase fancy things. I farm the way that keeps the land steady and the household safe. Cotton is still my main crop, because in our place I’ve grown it many years and I know how to handle it. But I still keep some wheat and maize on part of the land, because grain in hand makes people feel settled, and if cotton price is no good, at least we still have something. I only finished primary school, so I don’t count too finely. I mostly look at what happened last year, how the soil looks, whether there is enough cash, and what the neighbors are doing. Some people in the family work outside, so labor at home is not as full as before. I can still do the lighter work, but for heavy work and busy days I may need family help or hire a little.

This year I’ll keep most land in cotton, about 10 mu, and use 8 mu for wheat followed by summer maize. Cotton takes longer, but I know it well. Wheat-maize is our old safe way. For fertilizer, I won’t cut too hard. If I save too much on fertilizer and the crop turns weak, then I lose more. But I also won’t push too high, because pumping water costs money and I need to leave some cash in hand. I have well water, so if spring is dry or wheat needs water at jointing, I can irrigate. Cotton I’ll water only when it really needs it. Maize in summer depends partly on rain, so if rain is decent I won’t irrigate much.
